<!-- The abstract is a single paragraph, in the order of the paper: question,
     what was done, what was found, what it means. It is rendered BEFORE the
     Methods run the analysis, so inline R here would find no results yet:
     write its numbers by hand once the results are final, or keep it, as
     here, to what does not change when the data do.
     The keywords go on the last line, after "**Keywords:**", all on that one
     line: every render reads them from there, and so do the summary and the
     deposit. -->

Tropical forests hold many tree species, and which of them grow together
changes from place to place within a forest. We asked whether the number of
tree species and the composition of the tree assemblage differ among the
habitats of the forest of Barro Colorado Island, Panama, with the trees of
its 50-ha plot as the vegan package distributes them. Species richness was
modelled with a Poisson generalized linear model, and composition was compared
among habitats with a PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with a test
of the homogeneity of their dispersions (PERMDISP) and a non-metric
multidimensional scaling. How strongly habitat structures the forest, and
which species dominate it, are reported with their uncertainty. The analysis
is a worked example: every number in the text, the figures and the tables is
computed from the data when the manuscript is rendered.

**Keywords:** Barro Colorado Island, beta diversity, NMDS, PERMANOVA, tropical trees
